opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation.
opportunities.summary: Funds the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to focus on data analysis and synthesis, fostering collaboration and mentoring.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: up to £500 per year for a decade; first five years' funding of £3,500 claimable in year 1, additional £3,500 in year 6

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funds research on education methods within ecology to improve teaching and learning practices, providing up to £5,000 towards evidence-based learning.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funds placements (secondments) of up to 12 months that immerse an ecologist in another discipline or sector to develop interdisciplinary skills, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required; open to researchers from all countries globally; not available to cover principal researcher salary, bench fees or departmental vehicle hire.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; projects must be aimed at a non-academic audience.
opportunities.summary: Funds independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: maximum £500 for in-person events, maximum £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher; work/study at a university or research institution; work in scientific areas within ecology remit.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to present their work at workshops and conferences.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must have applied to present at the BES Annual Meeting; at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering travel and related costs.
